conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale** (EPDS). It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, because the postpartum weeks can bring more ups and downs than most people expect. Everything you share stays confidential between you and your care team, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. We’ll go through ten questions about the past seven days; most moms finish in just a few minutes. Ready to start?

**Question 1**  
Over the last week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things—would you say always, most of the time, sometimes, or hardly ever?
Sometimes... I can still laugh if something's really funny, but it feels kind of forced, like I'm not getting the same lift from it that I used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’m sorry… did you want me to pick one of the choices again? I said “sometimes,” but if you need me to be clearer: I laugh, but it doesn’t come easily—so “sometimes” fits best.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not very often. I’ll make plans—like meeting a friend for coffee or taking the baby for a walk—but when the time comes I feel kind of flat, like I’m just going through the motions instead of really looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I jump straight to thinking it’s something I did—like I’m not feeding him right or I missed his sleepy cues. Most of the time I know it’s probably not my fault, but the guilty thought still pops up first.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, pretty often. I’ll be sitting there with the baby sleeping soundly, but my mind races about whether he’s breathing okay or if I sterilized the bottles right. There’s no real reason, but the worry just barges in and it’s hard to shut it off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes—maybe a couple of times this week. Out of nowhere my heart starts racing and I get this tight, shaky feeling, like something awful is about to happen, even though nothing’s going on. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days feel like I’m barely treading water. I’ll start one chore, the baby cries, and suddenly everything piles up—dishes, laundry, messages I haven’t answered—and I feel like I’m failing at all of it. I usually get through, but it’s overwhelming more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling through “what-ifs” about the baby, things I should’ve done, stuff I might mess up tomorrow. It takes me ages to drift off, and I wake up a couple of times with my mind racing again.
I have felt sad or miserable
Pretty often. It’s like a gray cloud that rolls in and just hangs there. I can still smile for the baby or if someone visits, but underneath I feel heavy and down most of the day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened maybe twice this week. I’ll be feeding the baby or just sitting on the couch and the tears start. Nothing huge triggered it—I just feel overwhelmed and sad and the crying kind of leaks out.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I… yeah, it has, just for a moment. Once or twice when everything felt too heavy, I had this quick flash of “what if I weren’t here,” but I don’t want to act on it—I love my baby and want to be okay for him. It’s scary that the thought even shows up, though.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Postpartum Depression Screening – Brief Summary  
Date: [today]

Patient-reported symptoms (10-item EPDS-style inquiry):

- Persistent low mood, “heavy and down most of the day,” with tearfulness ×2 this week  
- Marked anhedonia—plans made but experienced as “flat,” minimal anticipatory enjoyment  
- Excessive self-blame/guilt re infant care (“guilty thought pops up first”)  
- Daily free-floating anxiety, intrusive “what-ifs,” occasional panic-like episodes (HR racing, shaky)  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed (“barely treading water”) most days  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance problems driven by ruminative worry  
- Fleeting passive self-harm cognitions (“what if I weren’t here”) without intent or plan; patient explicitly rejects acting on them

Pattern: Symptoms present “pretty often” to “most days,” beginning post-delivery; no prior psychiatric history reported per today’s inquiry.

Screening significance  
– EPDS total indicative of likely major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety features  
– Safety: presence of self-harm ideation (even if transient) → elevated risk; requires formal risk assessment and safety planning

Recommendations  
– Prompt referral to perinatal mental health specialist for diagnostic evaluation, risk assessment, and discussion of evidence-based treatment options  
– Provide crisis/safety resources before departure

Clinician: [Name, Credentials]  
Duration: ~10 min
